clue.text: Thus a cad dressed to make a stylish impression

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters are rearranged into a new outfit, so the words are reworked

explanation.surface: A bounder puts on fine clothes to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is an idiom for looking impressively stylish.

clue.text: TV programme after tea: Mum in Drag'

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other, here within the word for haul

parts.note: to tow is to drag
mum and sh both mean keep quiet

explanation.surface: Teatime television featuring a mother dressed up as a drag act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: CHA comes first. Mum here means silence, as in 'mum's the word'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a television programme of celebrity interviews.

clue.text: Where to find orchestra upset over largely insignificant composer

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed on top of the next piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a theatre orchestra plays in the pit

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: petty means insignificant

explanation.surface: A minor composer upsets the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PIT to TIP; 'largely' cuts PETTY to PETT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Michael Tippett was an English twentieth-century composer.

clue.text: Liberal peer's rise is amusing

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the letters go upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a lord is a peer

explanation.surface: A Liberal member of the House of Lords enjoys a funny elevation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses LLORD in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means dryly humorous.

clue.text: Conspicuous when refusing to comply

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means prominent, and also persisting in resistance or refusal.

clue.text: A fine, honest business

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
fair means honest or just

explanation.surface: Praise for a reputable enterprise that is also excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean a matter or concern, as in 'that's my business'.

clue.text: Rights to show endless soccer competition: fifty matches!

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: the FA Cup is the English football competition
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
ties are matches in a cup competition

explanation.surface: Broadcast rights for a football tournament with fifty games.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty can be a granted licence or power, especially in church law, hence a right.

clue.text: His love letters were sent out of order

definitions.text: His love letters were sent out of order

parts.words: His love letters were sent out of order
parts.note: the medieval philosopher whose love letters with Heloise are famous, while 'out of order' also hints at the monastic order

explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as being about the famous medieval letters between a scholar-monk and Heloise.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard, the French scholar, exchanged celebrated love letters with Heloise.

clue.text: Note small particle at some distance

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
a mote is a speck of dust

explanation.surface: A tiny speck is noticed far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote means far off, distant.

clue.text: Sanction a paper, oddly elliptical

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the word paper

parts.note: an oval is an elliptical shape

explanation.surface: A document gets a strange, cryptic endorsement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanction as a noun is official permission or endorsement.

clue.text: Laugh-how many people react to Hammer movie?

definitions.meaning: something very funny is a laugh, or a riot

definitions.text: how many people react to Hammer movie?
definitions.meaning: Hammer Films made British horror pictures, which make audiences shriek

explanation.walkthrough: Hammer was a British studio famous for horror films.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilarious person or event is called a scream, and a shriek of fright is the horror-film reaction.

clue.text: Female will attack

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
'll is the contracted form of will

explanation.surface: A woman announces she is about to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell is to bombard with artillery, an assault.

clue.text: Chemical sprayed in trees, not a field, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A crop spray turns up in woodland rather than on farmland, unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf-stripping agent such as Agent Orange is sprayed on forests to remove foliage.

clue.text: Move on quickly, placing foreign minor in secure hospital room

indicators.note: in means placed inside, here between the two words

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, secure
a ward is a room in a hospital
For. is the short, minor form of foreign

explanation.surface: Hurriedly admitting a child from abroad to a locked hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign minor' means the abbreviated form of foreign, FOR, set inside FASTWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance a recording rapidly ahead, as on a tape player.

clue.text: No longer being thought of as mad?

definitions.meaning: something forgotten has left your thoughts

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means insane, and read literally it means no longer in your thoughts, i.e. forgotten.

clue.text: Patriot seen to lose energy and falter

parts.note: to flag is to tire
to waver is to falter

explanation.surface: A patriot is seen to tire and hesitate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who waves the national flag is a zealous nationalist.

clue.text: Writer of detective stories is not mad to swallow tablet

indicators.note: to swallow is to take inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: sane means not mad
a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: A crime novelist, perfectly sane, takes a pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Spillane was an American crime novelist, creator of Mike Hammer.

clue.text: Carpet: hurriedly produce a long, narrow piece

parts.note: to tear off a letter is to dash it off quickly
a strip is a long, narrow piece

explanation.surface: Instructions for cutting a runner rug quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: To carpet someone is British slang for to reprimand them, the verb sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to scold someone severely, a British idiom for a dressing-down.

clue.text: Fooled-made to look small?

definitions.meaning: a garment ... is altered to be narrower

explanation.definitionFit: To be deceived, and of clothes, to be narrowed by a tailor.

clue.text: Recipe: put small quantity of vinegar in garlic mayonnaise for a square meal?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe on prescriptions

indicators.note: in means one goes inside, here within the sauce

parts.note: aioli is garlic mayonnaise

indicators.note: small quantity of means just the initial letter is taken

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: add a dash of vinegar to the garlic sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small quantity of' gives V, the first letter of vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are square pasta parcels, a witty play on 'square meal'.

clue.text: Escape using stairs

definitions.meaning: a set of steps between floors

explanation.definitionFit: Flight means fleeing, and a staircase is a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Be fond of drink in copious amounts

parts.note: to like is to be fond of
water is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone who loves a tipple in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending money like water means lavishly, in great abundance.

clue.text: Carp caught by a villager after forsaking booze

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: forsaking means abandoning, so the drink's letters are dropped from villager

parts.note: lager is a type of booze

explanation.surface: A fish is landed by a rustic once he has given up drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forsaking' removes LAGER from VILLAGER, leaving VIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to make petty objections, to quibble.

clue.text: Swim like utter novice in class

indicators.note: in means one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
raw means inexperienced, like a complete beginner

explanation.surface: A complete beginner learns a stroke in a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is a swimming stroke, front crawl.

clue.text: Conventional city supplies information on girl

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A town provides details about a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss city gave its name to the Geneva Conventions, so it is a convention city.

clue.text: A pain or a nervous disorder?

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery, agitated letters, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried person wonders whether their ache is real or a mental condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal for APAINORA.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoia is a mental condition marked by irrational suspicion.

clue.text: Sacred writings discovered in distant Rangoon

indicators.note: discovered in means found within these words, so the letters are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Holy texts turn up in faraway Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantras are Hindu and Buddhist religious texts.

clue.text: Personal assistant mostly put off entering Australian city

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an aide is a personal assistant

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to delay is to put off

explanation.surface: A secretary nearly postpones arriving in a city Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DELAY to DELA, and 'entering' places it inside AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the state capital of South Australia.
